result_json.message: review: plan 216 phase 3 migration commands and records

items.title: migrate-schema captures expectedKeys after the subject read, so concurrent migrations and lineage writes pass the precondition
items.reason: Plan requires expectedKeys over budget, steps, and decisions so a concurrent decision or competing digest fails with RECORD_PRECONDITION_FAILED and the command never applies twice. migratePlanSchema reads the subject (migrations, parentLineageId, replayed sourceBytes), awaits a git read, and only then captures keys in executePlanSchemaMigration, so writes in that window become part of the expected baseline.
items.failure: Two operators run migrate-schema with different targets: both read no migration, B appends, A captures keys including B's records and appends a second migration; replay treats two migrations as an invalid chain and the run is permanently drift-blocked. A text amendment landing in the window likewise yields a stale parentLineageId/beforeBlobHash.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Capture the three key lists before readSchemaMigrationSubject (or derive migrations and lineage from the same captured budget lines) and add a race unit test expecting RECORD_PRECONDITION_FAILED and one migration.

introducedBy.explanation: The new schema-migration.ts reads the subject in migratePlanSchema, awaits showPlanAtCommit, and only then calls recordStore.listLines for steps, budget, and decisions inside executePlanSchemaMigration to build expectedKeys.

items.mechanicalExplanation: Mirror recover-plan (implementation-recovery.ts lines 175-181): capture steps, budget, and decisions keys before reading the lineage and subject, and pass them into executePlanSchemaMigration.

items.title: Execution-run migration refused whenever the source run has any migration, blocking the plan's path for a pre-existing binding
items.reason: The plan says a source migration does not attach to an existing execution binding and the operator runs the command on the execution run. Bind always applies a valid source migration, so the sourceMigrations clause only affects bindings that predate the source migration, which is exactly that sanctioned path.
items.failure: Execution run binds the schema 0 approval; operator later migrates the source run; the execution run's status edit drifts and migrate-schema --run <execution> returns PLAN_MIGRATION_CONFLICT. Append-only records leave no migration path for that run.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Remove the clause (and the unused sourceMigrations field) and add a bind-then-source-migrate-then-execution-migrate unit test expecting created: true.

introducedBy.explanation: This hunk adds SchemaMigrationSubject.sourceMigrations and populates it for execution subjects from listPlanSchemaMigrations(binding.sourceRunId); the new executePlanSchemaMigration conflict check adds (input.subject.kind === "execution" && input.subject.sourceMigrations.length > 0), which refuses the execution-run migration the plan prescribes when a binding predates a source migration.

items.mechanicalExplanation: Drop the subject.kind === 'execution' && sourceMigrations.length > 0 clause; bindingPlanSchema === 1 and migrations.length > 0 already cover every case the plan lists.

items.title: plan migrate --mode selective --write rewrites identical bytes and reports wrote: true with unchanged: true
items.reason: Selective mode never transforms the file, yet writes it and reports wrote: true, contradicting unchanged: true.
items.failure: Operator output says the file was written when nothing changed, and the file mtime is bumped.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Delete the selective writeFileSync and return wrote: false.

introducedBy.explanation: The new handler's selective branch calls writeFileSync(absolute, raw) and returns wrote: write while unchanged: true.

items.mechanicalExplanation: Skip the write and return wrote: false, matching equivalent mode's write && !unchanged rule.
